title: WIP: css variable calc minification
author: MoritzLoewenstein
summary: Draft from 2023 that rewrites calc() token lists inside custom property values (unwrap single-arg calc, turn nested calc into parens). Abandoned (author said they lack Rust experience), works on raw tokens rather than the calc parser, and unwrapping calc() in custom properties isn't safe in general since the value is substituted as tokens.
evidence: Draft, no commits since 2023; author 2023-10-22: "I was struggling to implement the more useful transforms because I dont have any rust experience". master 574eee2 CLI --minify keeps `--foo:calc(1px)` unchanged. Removing calc() inside a custom property changes the token stream that var() substitutes and what getPropertyValue / style() container queries see, so it would need careful design. No maintainer engagement.
draft:
Thanks for exploring this, and sorry it sat for so long! Since this has been a draft for a while, I'm going to close it. Simplifying `calc()` inside custom properties is trickier than it looks: the value is substituted as tokens wherever `var(--foo)` is used, and `getPropertyValue('--foo')` and style queries see it as written, so turning `calc(1px)` into `1px` isn't always a no-op. If someone wants to pick this up again, it would need to reuse the existing calc parser rather than rewriting tokens, so it can be sure the result means the same thing.
